//: Configuration for a Tiny Tapeout micro tile container on ihp-sg13cmos5l:
a 1x1 project (202.08 x 154.98 um) holding four 86.40 x 68.04 um micro tiles.
CLOCK_PERIOD - Increase this in case you are getting setup time violations.
The value is in nanoseconds, so 20ns == 50MHz.
Hold slack margin - Increase them in case you are getting hold violations.
RUN_LINTER, LINTER_INCLUDE_PDK_MODELS - Disabling the linter is not recommended!
The micro tiles sit in the four corners of the tile, with their signal pins facing a
29.28 um wide channel in the middle (the right column is mirrored). Their left, right and
bottom margins overlap the margins of the container. The mux logic goes in the channel
and in the three rows above the micro tiles, below the pins of the container.
Keep the container's standard cells (and their Metal1 rails) clear of the micro tiles.
The vertical halo also removes the row right above the micro tiles.
Power: the micro tiles have horizontal Metal3 power stripes. The container's vertical
Metal4 stripes run over the micro tiles; setting PDN_HORIZONTAL_LAYER to Metal3 makes the
macro grid add Via3 arrays wherever a Metal4 stripe crosses a Metal3 stripe of the same
net. (The container itself has no horizontal stripes: PDN_MULTILAYER is off.)
Vertical Metal4 stripes: VPWR at x = 6, 36, ... 186 and VGND at x = 15.6, 45.6, ... 195.6.
Every micro tile gets three stripes of each net, and the channel between them one of each.
The micro tiles own Metal1, Metal2 and Metal3 inside their area, except for the 1 um strip
along the channel where their signal pins are. Metal4 over the micro tiles stays available.
Save some time
Don't put clock buffers on the outputs
Reduce wasted space
Absolute die size
Clock
Don't generate power rings
MAGIC_DEF_LABELS may cause issues with LVS
Only export pin area in LEF (without any connected nets)
